user.title: Sign in to Aqara
user.description:
Aqara FP2 Companion finds every FP2 paired through HomeKit Device by itself. Sign in with the Aqara account that holds them.

If the AppDaemon app of Aqara FP2 Companion is still installed, remove it first: the two must not share the Aqara session.

data_description.account: The email or phone number you sign in to the Aqara app with.
data_description.password: Used once to sign in. Only the session is kept, never the password.
data_description.country: The one chosen in the Aqara app. It decides which Aqara servers hold the account.
data_description.app_identity: Only for an account in the China region, as app_id:app_key. Leave empty otherwise.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Aqara again
reauth_confirm.description: Aqara ended the session, so the settings and zones of the FP2s cannot be read or changed. Sign in again.

init.title: Aqara FP2 Companion settings
init.description: FP2s paired through HomeKit are found automatically. Change these only if you need to.

data.backups_keep: Zone backups to keep per device

data_description.devices: For FP2s that aren't paired through HomeKit. One serial per field, like 54EF44A1B2C3.
data_description.exclude: These FP2s are ignored, even if HomeKit finds them. One serial per field, like 54EF44A1B2C3.
data_description.backups_keep: A backup is saved when the zones change and before every zone write. Older ones are deleted.
data_description.token_check_time: The Aqara token is checked every day at this time and refreshed if it expires within 3 days.
data_description.app_identities: Optional, as app_id:app_key. Saved credentials aren't shown. Leave this empty to keep them, or enter new ones to replace them.

error.clear_and_replace: Either delete the saved credentials or enter new ones, not both.

appdaemon_app_installed.title: The AppDaemon app of Aqara FP2 Companion is still installed
appdaemon_app_installed.description:
Aqara FP2 Companion now runs as an integration, and the AppDaemon app is still in `{path}`. If AppDaemon runs it, the app and the integration would both act on every card command and refresh the same Aqara session, signing each other out. So the integration waits.

First stop AppDaemon, or remove the `fp2_companion` entry from its `apps.yaml` and restart it, so that the app is no longer running. Then delete that folder. The old session in `/share/appdaemon/fp2_companion/` is deleted by the integration once it has copied it. The integration then starts by itself, keeps your Aqara session and your zone backups, and this repair goes away.
